brief: b11 moved the sun and nothing anybody DOES followed it. sunUp/sunDown now swing from 7.00/18.50 in midwinter to 4.00/21.50 in midsummer, while the town's working day is still nailed to the clock: kioskOpen() 7.5-18.5, marketActive() 8-17, marketRaise putting stalls up from 6.90 and taking them down from 17.00, the sweeper at 5.00-6.50, the wind announcement between 7 and 9. So in midwinter the traders raise three stalls and the sweeper works the courtyard in the dark an hour before dawn, and in midsummer the kiosk shuts with three hours of daylight left and the market packs away in full sun. Put the working day on the sun. timeLabel() is the model and it is already in the file — hung off sunUp/sunDown at #12 with a comment saying otherwise 'the label reads Morning in the winter dark' — and nobody carried the idea past the label. Keep each interval's RELATION to sunrise and sunset rather than its number.
successLooksLike: Nobody in this town starts work in the dark on any day of the year, and the long summer evening gets used. A probe at four seasons shows the market's raise window and the kiosk's hours sitting at a constant offset from sunUp/sunDown while their clock times move by hours.
avoid: Do not stretch marketActive() so far that market day loses its shape — it is nine hours now, and a winter market that runs four is a different feature; set a floor. LAW: when you turn a constant into a variable, grep for everything tuned against the old number — the 17.00 pack-away is also read by the market-closed announcement near line 3745, and marketRaise's down window has to stay inside whatever marketActive() becomes.
